skill.name: nano-banana-builder
skill.description: Build full-stack web applications powered by Google Gemini Nano Banana image generation APIs. Use this skill for Next.js image generators, editors, galleries, storage, rate limits, and deployment patterns.
skill.summary: Build Next.js image generation apps with Gemini Nano Banana models.
skill.author: CesarAugustusGroB

content.value_statement: Image generation apps need correct model choices, storage, and quota handling. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through production Next.js patterns.
actual_capabilities: Provides exact Gemini image model names and selection guidance.
Shows server actions and API routes for image generation workflows.
Explains iterative editing, galleries, and multi-image composition patterns.
Covers Vercel Blob, S3, and base64 storage options.
Includes rate limiting, caching, retries, and cost control examples.
limitations: It provides implementation guidance, not a complete installed application.
Examples require valid Gemini and storage service credentials.
Quota, price, and model availability can change after publication.
Generated image safety still depends on provider policy enforcement.

use_cases.title: Prototype an Image Generator
use_cases.description: Create a simple Next.js text-to-image flow with a server action and model selection.

use_cases.title: Launch an Editing Tool
use_cases.description: Build an iterative editor that preserves image history and supports conversational changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare for Production
use_cases.description: Add object storage, rate limits, caching, retries, and user-friendly error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Generator
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Next.js page that generates one image from a text prompt using Gemini Nano Banana.

prompt_templates.title: Add Model Selection
prompt_templates.scenario: Let users choose speed or quality.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a model selector for Nano Banana and Nano Banana Pro, with clear labels and server-side model mapping.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Editing History
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an iterative image editor that stores the current image, edit prompts, and recent conversation history.

prompt_templates.title: Harden for Production
prompt_templates.prompt: Add object storage, rate limiting, retry handling, cache keys, and safe environment variable usage to this image app.

output_examples.input: Request a small image generator with fast drafts and final high quality output.
output_examples.output: A Next.js implementation plan with model mapping, server actions, and a compact generation interface.

output_examples.input: Ask for an editor that lets users refine an uploaded image in several steps.
output_examples.output: A component and API design that tracks the active image, edit prompt, and recent history.

output_examples.input: Prepare an app for production traffic and image storage.
output_examples.output: A deployment checklist covering environment variables, Blob or S3 storage, rate limits, caching, and retry behavior.

best_practices: Use the exact Gemini image model names from the skill.
Keep API keys on the server and read them from environment variables.
Store generated images in object storage and save URLs in the app.
anti_patterns: Do not invent Gemini image model names or add date suffixes.
Do not place provider API keys in client-side code.
Do not trigger paid generation on every prompt keystroke.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides an AI coding agent to build apps that call Gemini image APIs.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it target?
faq.answer: The examples focus on Next.js, React, server actions, and API routes.

faq.question: Can it help with image editing workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes iterative editing, multi-turn history, and composition patterns.

faq.question: Does it cover production operations?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes storage, rate limits, caching, retries, and error handling.

faq.question: Are credentials included in the skill?
faq.answer: No. The files show placeholder environment variable names only.
